terms.gloss: more, any more (of something offered again)

terms.grammar: noun in the singular, with a partitive genitive
evidence: Cic. Sen. 66: eō plūs viāticī quaerere
Publil. Sent. C 22: plūs vult quam licet
terms.comment: “More of” a thing is plūs with a genitive: plūs viāticī, more provisions; “more than”, plūs quam. With verbs and adjectives, see more (to a greater degree).

terms.gloss: more (in number): more people, more things
evidence: Cic. Fam. 7.6.2: sed plūra scrībēmus aliās

phrases.english: it is good. I ask for nothing more
but I’ll write more another time
the success of the wicked lures more people on

phrases.latin: Cui plūs licet quam pār est, plūs vult quam licet.
phrases.english: Allow someone more than is fair, and he wants more than is allowed.

sources: Lewis & Short: amplus · Lewis & Short: plus
Quotations from the Latinitas loci collections (loci-horatius, loci-cicero-epistulae, loci-phaedrus, loci-publilius, loci-cicero-philosophica), checked against the editions named there.
Publilius is cited as the loci collection numbers him, by position under each initial letter in the Latin Library text; from N onwards that numbering differs from Meyer’s.
The example sentences marked “composed” are ours.
